split_reasoning: This is one cross-cutting activity of following dangerous-goods safety procedures during transport.

parts.text: Follow required safety procedures when transporting dangerous goods.
parts.type_reasoning: The procedures are applied in hands-on transport work rather than producing a separate deliverable.

notes: Safety procedures vary by cargo and can be embedded in driving, securing loads, inspection and documentation.

split_reasoning: Checking the vehicle and its equipment is one inspection activity.

parts.text: Inspect the vehicle and its mechanical, safety and emergency equipment for working condition.
parts.type_reasoning: The inspection requires hands-on checks around the vehicle.

notes: Reporting defects is separately covered by task 10644.

split_reasoning: Hours-of-service logs and vehicle service or repair status logs are different records maintained for different purposes.

parts.text: Maintain a compliant log of working hours.
parts.type_reasoning: The driver completes a log record that others rely on for compliance.
parts.unit_reasoning: A daily hours-of-service record is a practical unit reviewed as a whole.
parts.start: duty-status information becomes available during the workday
parts.end: the day's log is completed and certified
parts.checked_by: carrier compliance staff and roadside inspectors

parts.text: Maintain a log of vehicle service or repair status.
parts.type_reasoning: Each status entry creates a record for maintenance and compliance staff.
parts.unit_reasoning: A service or repair status update is recorded and relied on as an individual entry.
parts.work_item: one vehicle service or repair status entry
parts.start: service or repair status information becomes available
parts.end: the status is entered in the vehicle log
parts.checked_by: maintenance staff and carrier compliance staff

notes: Shares depend on carrier procedures and how much maintenance logging the driver performs.

split_reasoning: Obtaining delivery acknowledgment and collecting payment are different activities performed at delivery.

parts.text: Obtain a receipt or signature acknowledging delivered goods.
parts.type_reasoning: The acknowledgment is obtained from the recipient during the delivery contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: A signed or otherwise acknowledged delivery document is the handoff for one delivery.
parts.start: the driver presents the delivery document to the recipient
parts.end: the recipient signs or provides a receipt and the driver has the acknowledgment
parts.checked_by: the recipient and the carrier's delivery or billing staff

parts.text: Collect payment for delivery services when required.
parts.type_reasoning: Payment is collected from the customer during the delivery contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: One payment collected and confirmed is the transaction relied on by billing staff.
parts.start: payment is requested or presented at delivery
parts.end: payment is accepted and acknowledged to the customer
parts.checked_by: the customer and the carrier's billing staff

notes: The payment share depends on how often the carrier requires payment at delivery.

split_reasoning: Positioning the truck for loading or unloading is one maneuver, using signals and position checks.

parts.text: Maneuver and position the truck for loading or unloading.
parts.type_reasoning: Positioning the vehicle is physical driving work at the loading site.

split_reasoning: Driving a heavy truck to transport cargo is one physical transport activity.

parts.text: Drive a heavy truck or tractor-trailer to transport and deliver cargo.
parts.type_reasoning: Driving requires operating the vehicle in the physical environment.

split_reasoning: The listed ropes, blocks, chains, binders and covers are alternative means of securing cargo.

parts.text: Secure cargo for transport using suitable restraints or covers.
parts.type_reasoning: Securing cargo requires hands-on work with the load and restraints.

split_reasoning: Reading a bill of lading to understand the assignment is one activity.

parts.text: Read the bill of lading to determine assignment details.
parts.type_reasoning: Reading the existing document for the driver's own understanding does not itself produce a separate item for others to check.

notes: Checking documentation for completeness and accuracy is separately covered by task 20693.

split_reasoning: Defects, accidents, violations and damage are different report subjects but use the same incident-reporting activity.

parts.text: Report a vehicle defect, accident, traffic violation or vehicle damage.
parts.type_reasoning: Each reported issue produces information that the carrier uses to act on the event.
parts.unit_reasoning: An individual issue or incident is reported and handled as a whole.
parts.work_item: one vehicle or driving incident report
parts.start: the driver identifies a defect or an incident occurs
parts.end: the required details are reported to the carrier or other designated recipient
parts.checked_by: supervisor, maintenance staff or carrier safety staff

notes: Reports may be written or transmitted verbally, depending on the carrier and event.

split_reasoning: Reading and interpreting maps are means of determining a route, not separate activities.

parts.text: Use maps to determine a suitable vehicle route.
parts.type_reasoning: The selected route is a distinct plan that the driver uses for the trip.
parts.unit_reasoning: A route for one trip or trip segment is the usable result of the map work.
parts.work_item: one map-based route for a trip or trip segment
parts.start: origin, destination and relevant route constraints are known
parts.end: a route is selected for use
parts.checked_by: the driver and, when shared, dispatch

notes: The route may be a mental or marked-up plan rather than a document sent to dispatch.

split_reasoning: Connecting or disconnecting the listed components are steps in coupling or uncoupling a trailer.

parts.text: Couple or uncouple a trailer, including its landing gear, lines and fifth-wheel lock.
parts.type_reasoning: The task requires hands-on manipulation of the tractor and trailer equipment.

split_reasoning: Collecting and verifying instructions and routes is one activity that produces a usable set of delivery instructions.

parts.text: Collect and verify delivery instructions and routes from the appropriate sources.
parts.type_reasoning: The resulting verified instructions are a distinct set of information used to make a delivery.
parts.unit_reasoning: Instructions are gathered and verified for an individual delivery assignment.
parts.start: a delivery assignment requires instructions or clarification
parts.end: the relevant instructions and route are obtained and verified for use
parts.checked_by: the driver and dispatch or the delivery site when clarification is needed

notes: Instructions may be received verbally or in writing; this item concerns obtaining and verifying them rather than a separate route-planning exercise.

split_reasoning: Inspecting an unloaded trailer for damage is one physical inspection activity.

parts.text: Inspect an unloaded trailer for damage.
parts.type_reasoning: The driver physically checks the trailer after unloading.

notes: Reporting any damage is separately covered by task 10644.

split_reasoning: Raising or lowering landing gear are alternative directions of the same equipment operation.

parts.text: Crank trailer landing gear up or down to secure the vehicle.
parts.type_reasoning: Cranking landing gear is hands-on physical work.

notes: Landing-gear operation is also a step in some coupling and uncoupling work.

split_reasoning: Adding fluids, making minor repairs and washing the truck are different kinds of maintenance work.

parts.text: Add fuel, oil or other vehicle fluids.
parts.type_reasoning: Replenishing fluids requires hands-on work at the vehicle.

parts.text: Perform minor vehicle repairs.
parts.type_reasoning: Minor repairs require hands-on work on vehicle components.

parts.text: Wash the truck.
parts.type_reasoning: Washing is physical cleaning work on the vehicle.

notes: Shares vary substantially by carrier and vehicle. Task 10662 overlaps with minor repairs when they are performed as emergency roadside repairs.

split_reasoning: Checking quantity and condition are components of the same inspection and inventory of goods to be moved.

parts.text: Inventory and inspect goods to be moved for quantity and condition.
parts.type_reasoning: Counting and inspecting the goods requires physical examination of the load.

notes: Any separate damage or discrepancy report is not specified by this target.

split_reasoning: Removing debris from loaded trailers is one cleaning activity.

parts.text: Remove debris from a loaded trailer.
parts.type_reasoning: Removing debris requires hands-on work in or around the trailer.

split_reasoning: Checking refrigeration equipment and providing food or water to livestock are different cargo-care activities.

parts.text: Check refrigeration systems for temperature-sensitive cargo.
parts.type_reasoning: Checking the refrigeration system involves physical inspection of equipment on the vehicle.

parts.text: Provide food or water to livestock in transit.
parts.type_reasoning: Feeding and watering livestock requires hands-on care.

notes: Shares depend on the mix of refrigerated and livestock hauling.

split_reasoning: Giving directions to packing and loading laborers is one supervisory interaction.

parts.text: Direct laborers packing goods and moving them onto trailers.
parts.type_reasoning: The work consists of live direction to the laborers rather than a separate deliverable.

split_reasoning: Installing and removing the listed special equipment are related hands-on equipment-change activities.

parts.text: Install or remove special vehicle equipment such as chains, blades or sanders.
parts.type_reasoning: Installing or removing equipment requires physical manipulation of vehicle hardware.

notes: Installing chains during an emergency roadside repair also falls under task 10662.

split_reasoning: The examples are different methods of performing the same general activity of emergency roadside repair.

parts.text: Perform emergency roadside repairs or install needed roadside equipment.
parts.type_reasoning: Roadside repair and installation require hands-on work on the vehicle.

split_reasoning: The listed systems and purposes are alternative uses of the same activity of operating auxiliary or idle-reduction power.

parts.text: Operate idle-reduction or auxiliary power equipment for the truck's power or climate needs.
parts.type_reasoning: The driver physically operates vehicle equipment rather than producing a separate deliverable.

split_reasoning: Planning and adjusting a route are the same route-selection activity performed at different times, using alternative navigation tools.

parts.text: Plan or adjust a route for changing conditions and fuel efficiency using navigation equipment.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a selected or revised route for the trip.
parts.unit_reasoning: A route or route revision for one trip segment is the usable planning output.
parts.start: a trip requires a route or changing conditions require a revision
parts.end: a suitable route is selected for use
parts.checked_by: the driver and, when shared, dispatch

notes: The route may remain in the navigation device or be used by the driver without a separate written handoff.

split_reasoning: Inspecting cargo security is one load-checking activity.

parts.text: Inspect a load to ensure the cargo is secure.
parts.type_reasoning: The driver physically examines the cargo and its restraints.

notes: Securing or correcting the load is separately covered by tasks 10642 and 20697.

split_reasoning: Completeness and accuracy are two checks applied to the same load-documentation review.

parts.text: Check a load's documentation for completeness and accuracy.
parts.type_reasoning: The review produces a checked set of documents used for the load.
parts.unit_reasoning: The documents for one load are checked together for the assignment.
parts.start: load-related documents are received for review
parts.end: the documents are checked and discrepancies identified for correction
parts.checked_by: the driver, dispatch and receiving or compliance staff

notes: The target does not necessarily include correcting discrepancies or submitting a separate report.

split_reasoning: Driving to weigh stations before, after or during a trip is the same compliance-related driving activity.

parts.text: Drive the truck to required weigh stations before and after loading or along the route.
parts.type_reasoning: The task is physical operation of the truck to reach weigh stations.

notes: The target specifies driving to the stations, not preparation of a separate weight report.

split_reasoning: Information is exchanged both in live conversations and through written dispatch messages, which are different work products.

parts.text: Exchange necessary information with dispatch, supervisors or drivers in live calls or radio conversations.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in the live operational conversation with colleagues.

parts.text: Send necessary operational information to dispatch, supervisors or drivers in a written message.
parts.type_reasoning: A written operational message is a distinct item the recipient can rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: An individual operational update or request is sent and read as a whole.
parts.start: the driver has information to transmit or a written request to answer
parts.end: the message is sent to the intended recipient
parts.checked_by: dispatch, a supervisor or the receiving driver

notes: Shares depend on the carrier's mix of radio, phone and in-cab messaging.

split_reasoning: Loading and unloading are opposite directions of the same physical cargo-handling activity, with or without assistance.

parts.text: Load or unload a truck, or assist others with the work, using appropriate equipment.
parts.type_reasoning: Moving cargo and operating loading equipment require hands-on physical work.

split_reasoning: Wrapping and securing goods are related physical preparation steps for protecting and restraining the load.

parts.text: Wrap and secure goods using protective packing and restraints.
parts.type_reasoning: Wrapping and securing goods require hands-on work with packing materials and restraints.
